title: Pin + Rollback + Fallback UX — rough wires & copy
summary: Working draft exploring a single coherent flow for: (1) pinning a model version to an endpoint, (2) quick rollback, and (3) automated fallback routing. Includes low-fi wireframe descriptions, button/tooltip copy, error states, and grooming notes for backlog prioritization.
body:
Context and goal:
- Problem: customers pin model versions for predictability but need simple, low-friction controls to roll forward/rollback and to set fallback rules when capacity or quality changes occur. Current console mechanics are fragmented (catalog -> endpoint -> rollout) and customers tell us they’re confused about where to manage fallback and how safe rollbacks are.

Wireframe walkthrough (low-fi):
1) Endpoint Overview (list row expanded)
   - Left: endpoint name, active model(s) with small chip rows (e.g., "mosaic-7b-v1.3 (pinned)").
   - Middle: health + latency card (live metric sparkline).
   - Right: quick actions: [Pin model] [Deploy new] [Rollout history].
   - Copy snippets:
       * Chip hover tooltip: "Pinned model — serves all requests unless a traffic rule overrides."
       * Quick action label: "Pin model" (primary), tooltip: "Lock this endpoint to a specific model version for predictable outputs."

2) Pin model modal (single-step)
   - Header: "Pin a model version to <endpoint-name>"
   - Top: searchable model selector (model name + version + perf badges).
   - Middle: Pin options: radio buttons: ( ) Full pin (100% traffic) ( ) Pin with canary (X% -> 100% over Y minutes)
   - Secondary: checkbox "Enable automatic fallback if pinned model fails health checks" (default: on). Tooltip: "If the pinned model becomes unavailable or regresses, route to fallback model(s) defined on the endpoint."
   - Primary CTA: "Pin and close" Secondary: "Preview rollout"
   - Copy drafts:
       * Body note under selector: "Select the exact model version you want to pin. You can change this later or use rollback if needed."

3) Canary preview screen (in-modal)
   - Visual bar showing percent split with annotated knobs (editable): "Canary: 10% -> 100% over 30m"
   - Safety toggles: "Auto-revert on error spike" (threshold slider), "Pause if latency > Xms for 3 consecutive checks"
   - Copy: "Canaries let you validate behavior before full cutover. If checks fail we’ll revert to the previous stable model automatically."

4) Rollback flow (quick rollback)
   - Access: endpoint -> actions -> "Rollback" (exposed when at least one previous model exists)
   - Click triggers confirmation drawer (not a full modal): shows last N deployments with miniature diffs (tokens, latencies, regression flags).
   - Confirmation CTA: "Rollback to mosaic-7b-v1.2"; destructive hint: "This will redirect all traffic back to the selected model. Requests in-flight may finish on the previous model."
   - Undo affordance: toast with "Undo" for 30s and a link to rollback history.
   - Error state copy: on failure, "Rollback failed — a revalidation attempt is scheduled. If you need assistance, contact support or open INF-2410."

5) Fallback rules screen (per-endpoint sub-tab)
   - Simple rule builder: Add fallback model(s) ordered by priority; each entry: model + reason tags (e.g., OOM, latency, quality) + max traffic share when fallback active.
   - Sticky help line: "Fallbacks are only used when health checks fail or when a pinned model hits capacity limits."
   - Copy: empty state: "No fallback models defined. Add a fallback to keep your endpoint serving if the primary model becomes unavailable."

Error and edge case notes (from SRE triage):
- If pinned model is incompatible with endpoint config (e.g., sequence length), show inline validation preventing pin. Message: "Selected model requires seq_len > 4096 — update endpoint config or pick a compatible model."
- If auto-fallback is ON but no fallback models configured, show warning in pin modal: "Auto-fallback enabled but no fallback models set — requests may fail if the pinned model becomes unhealthy."
- Rollback collisions: if two users try to rollback simultaneously, lock and show "Rollback pending — another user is performing a rollback. Retry in 30s."

Grooming notes / acceptance criteria (rough):
- AC1: Pin modal should support full pin + canary options and persist choice in endpoint config.
- AC2: Auto-fallback checkbox must toggle a boolean on endpoint and be editable later.
- AC3: Quick rollback must complete in <10s for UI surface and create an audit trail entry.
- AC4: Fallback routing must respect priority and max-traffic share.

Backlog prioritization (rough estimates):
- M (0.5): Inline pin validation (blocker for many customers)
- L (1): Fallback UI list + add/remove (simple manage)
- M (2): Canary editor + safety toggles
- H (3): Quick rollback + audit trail + optimistic UI

Open questions / discussion items:
- Do we surface cost delta when pinning to a larger model? (request from finance/CS).
- Should fallback accept a weighted list (multi-fallback) or stop at first healthy model?
- How to expose cross-endpoint fallback (share fallback pools across endpoints)?

Prototype copy snippets (final candidate CTAs / microcopy):
- Primary pin CTA: "Pin and close"
- Canary CTA: "Start canary" / Secondary: "Schedule rollout"
- Rollback CTA: "Rollback to this version" / Undo toast: "Rollback undone"
- Fallback empty state: "Add a fallback model to keep requests healthy if the pinned model fails."

Notes for UX handoff (assets):
- Provide SVG of the canary percent bar and knob states (desktop + mobile).
- Include a tiny animation spec for canary ramp preview (~400ms ease).
- List of telemetry events required: pin_clicked, canary_started, rollback_initiated, fallback_triggered, fallback_used_count.

Conversation snippets to include in PR description:
- "We want a single clear place to manage model version guarantees (pin) and availability controls (fallback)." — Marcus
- "Make rollback easy and reversible; customers are scared of long downtime if a model regresses." — Elena

Reference links (internal):
- INF-2345: Pinning feature spec (high-level)
- INF-2410: Rollback incident runbook

Localization notes:
- Keep CTAs short (max 3 words) so they translate cleanly.
- Avoid idioms (e.g., "flip the switch") in confirmations.

Last thoughts (Priya):
- This is intentionally rough. Primary goal for next sprint: validate the modal flow with 2 customers and prototype the canary ramp control. We should avoid overloading the first iteration; MVP: full pin + auto-fallback toggle + simple rollback that hits the audit trail.
action_items: Add inline validation for seq_len mismatch — @Tom
